text.p: Pulte Corp said Tuesday it is reorganizing its homebuilding operations to strengthen management focus on key customer groups and to generate increased operating efficiencies.

The reorganization creates a new position of Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer with responsibility for all of Pulte's homebuilding businesses and appoints senior Pulte executives to head the company's domestic homebuilding and active adult/retirement operations.
Previously, Pulte's homebuilding operations were comprised of three geographically-based operating companies.

Pulte said it named Mark O'Brien, 54, as Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, in charge of all domestic and international homebuilding businesses as well as the company's active adult/retirement and manufactured housing operations.
Previously, O'Brien was president of Pulte Home East, with responsibility for the company's 23 homebuilding markets located in the north and southeastern regions of the United States.

"With the maturation of our newer homebuilding markets well underway, we are now in a position to transition to a structure, which will allow us to concentrate more effectively on our fast-growing customer segments and to leverage critical management processes and strategic initiatives throughout all of our operations," Robert Burgess, Pulte's president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Mr. Robert J. Halso, 46, assumes the role of President of Pulte's 40 domestic homebuilding markets. Mr. Halso, formerly the President of the Pulte Home Central operating company, also assumes responsibility for Pulte's highly successful Canterbury affordable housing communities.

Recognizing that a major portion of Pulte's future growth will arise from the housing and home services needs of homebuyers 50 years or older, Burgess also announced the formation of a new business entity that will develop larger scale adult/retirement communities on a national basis.
